title: Finite free kernels have finite chains with quasi-coherent ideal quotients
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], I a finite index type, and p: O_X^(I) → O_X a morphism of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There exist a natural number n and a sequence F_j of O_X-modules such that F_0 is a zero object, F_n is isomorphic to kernel p, and for every j < n there is an ideal sheaf datum J_j on X whose associated module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and arrows a_j: F_j → F_(j+1) and b_j: F_(j+1) → J_j.toModules forming a short exact sequence. There is no vanishing-cohomology, quasi-compactness, affineness or surjectivity assumption. Terms after n are unconstrained.

source.place: Tag 01XF, label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering, paragraph constructing F_i as the intersection with the first i direct summands; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XF

proof.text: Enumerate I by n coordinates. For 0 ≤ j ≤ n let F_j be the kernel of the restriction of p to the first j coordinate summands, and extend F_j constantly after n. The empty source gives IsZero F_0, and the enumeration induces F_n ≅ kernel p. Finite free modules and the structure sheaf are quasi-coherent; quasi-coherent kernel closure therefore gives quasi-coherence of F_j.

For j < n project F_(j+1) onto its last coordinate. Its sectionwise kernel is F_j: a vector with last coordinate zero is precisely a vector in the first j coordinates killed by p. Its abelian image is quasi-coherent by quasiCoherent_cokernel_image. On each affine open U, the sections of the image form an ideal J(U) in Γ(X,U). Quasi-coherence identifies their restrictions to D(f) with localizations; since image sections inject into the structure sheaf, the localized ideal equals the image of J(U) in Γ(X,D(f)). Thus these section ideals define IdealSheafData J.

The image module and J.toModules are isomorphic as subsheaves of O_X. To construct the comparison, their inclusions have the same ranges over each affine open: J.toModules has range J(U) by range_toModulesι_app and the image has range J(U) by construction. Since both inclusions are injective, these range equalities give mutually inverse linear section maps on affine opens. Uniqueness makes these maps commute with restrictions; sheaf gluing extends them to all opens. Transport quasi-coherence and the epimorphic image factorization along this isomorphism. The projection has kernel F_j, so its factorization onto its image gives the required short exact sequence. Nothing used Epi p; for I empty use n=0 and a constant zero chain.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_free_kernel_ideal_filtration (X : Scheme.{u})
    {I : Type u} [Finite I]
    (p : SheafOfModules.free (R := X.ringCatSheaf) I ⟶
      SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : ℕ → X.Modules),
      IsZero (F 0) ∧ Nonempty (F n ≅ kernel p) ∧
      ∀ j : ℕ, j < n → ∃ J : X.IdealSheafData,
        J.toModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
        ∃ (a : F j ⟶ F (j + 1)) (b : F (j + 1) ⟶ J.toModules)
          (w : a ≫ b = 0), (ShortComplex.mk a b w).ShortExact
